# p0_ai_gateway (Resource)

Final installation of an AI gateway, which hosts MCP servers and applies P0 access
policy to agent tool calls.

To use this resource, you must also install the `p0_ai_gateway_staged` resource, and configure your
gateway to trust the service account returned by that resource (e.g. the `manageAllowedEmails` value in the
`ai-gateway-stack` Helm chart).

See the example usage for the recommended pattern to define this infrastructure.

For the full install steps, see [Gateway](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/agentic-gateway/gateway).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# See the p0_ai_gateway_staged example for the preceding steps
# (staging the gateway, and configuring it to trust the assigned service
# account) that this resource depends on.

resource "p0_ai_gateway_staged" "example" {
  id = "primary"
  domain_hosting = {
    url = "https://gateway.example.com"
  }
}

# Uses the p0-security/p0-ai-gateway-stack/kubernetes module:
# https://github.com/p0-security/terraform-kubernetes-p0-ai-gateway-stack
module "ai_gateway_stack" {
  source  = "p0-security/p0-ai-gateway-stack/kubernetes"
  version = "1.3.0"

  chart_version = "1.3.0-beta"
  release_name  = p0_ai_gateway_staged.example.id
  namespace     = "p0-ai-gateway"

  values = [
    yamlencode({
      letsEncrypt = {
        env   = "prod"
        email = "admin@example.com"
      }
      postgresql   = { storageClass = "gp2" }
      victorialogs = { storageClass = "gp2" }
      valkey       = { storageClass = "<encrypted-storage-class>" }
      "ai-gateway" = {
        gateway = {
          className = p0_ai_gateway_staged.example.id
          host      = "gateway.example.com"
        }
        authServer = {
          oidcClientId = "your-upstream-oidc-client-id"
          gatewayIss   = "https://gateway.example.com"
        }
        accessProxy = {
          gatewayIss          = "https://gateway.example.com"
          manageAllowedEmails = p0_ai_gateway_staged.example.service_account_email
        }
      }
    }),
  ]
}

# Finalizes the install; depends_on ensures the gateway trusts P0's service
# account before verification is attempted.
resource "p0_ai_gateway" "example" {
  id = p0_ai_gateway_staged.example.id
  domain_hosting = {
    load_balancer_ip = "<your-gateway-loadbalancer-ip>"
  }
  log_project_id = "my-gcp-logging-project"
  # The contents of /p0-files/jwk.public.json in the braekhus-client pod
  braekhus_public_jwk = "<public-jwk-json>"
  depends_on          = [module.ai_gateway_stack]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `braekhus_public_jwk` (String) Public key (a JWK, the contents of `jwk.public.json`) that the gateway's outbound
management tunnel uses to authenticate to P0. Must be an EC P-384 public key; never supply the private key. With
the `ai-gateway-stack` chart, read it from the running gateway:
`kubectl -n <namespace> exec deploy/braekhus-client -- cat /p0-files/jwk.public.json`. P0 verifies the
gateway through that tunnel, so a gateway that is not publicly reachable can still be verified.
- `id` (String) The `id` of the `p0_ai_gateway_staged` resource being finalized

### Optional

- `domain_hosting` (Attributes) How this gateway's public hostname and DNS records are managed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--domain_hosting))
- `log_project_id` (String) GCP project ID where this gateway's Cloud Logging entries actually land, so P0 can show its
MCP tool-call and A2A activity. This is the project holding the log bucket, which may not be the same project the
gateway itself runs in (e.g. if logs are routed to a centralized logging project).

### Read-Only

- `service_account_email` (String) Email address of the service account identity that P0 uses to communicate with your gateway

<a id="nestedatt--domain_hosting"></a>
### Nested Schema for `domain_hosting`

Optional:

- `load_balancer_ip` (String) Your gateway's LoadBalancer address (IP or hostname). Create a DNS record for the `url` on the
`p0_ai_gateway_staged` resource pointing here: an A record for an IPv4 address, AAAA for IPv6, or CNAME
if your cloud provider (e.g. AWS) gave you a hostname instead of a static IP.
